rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj favors al-Shaʿbi’s explanation of the first pre-Islamic age because its people were known for keeping prostitutes.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الأشبه قول الشعبي، لأنهم هم الجاهلية المعروفون، كانوا يتخذون البغايا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a dialogue with ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas argues that calling one age the first implies it had a later counterpart.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: وهل كانت الأولى إلا ولها آخرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the later Jahiliyya as the period between Jesus and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والجاهلية الأخرى ما بين عيسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the first Jahiliyya to mean pre-Islamic disbelief and the later one sinful conduct within Islam, forbidding imitation of the former.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الجاهلية الأولى جاهلية الكفر قبل الإسلام، والجاهلية الأخرى جاهلية الفسوق والفجور في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report is attributed to the Prophet addressing Abu al-Darda about Jahiliyya, but Abū Ḥayyān corrects the familiar version: the addressee was Abū Dharr.
rows.anchor:
والمعروف
في الحديث أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إنما قال: «إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية» ، لأبي ذر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya takes the phrase to mean the pre-Islamic way of life alone, marked by little jealousy and women living without seclusion; first distinguishes it from Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والذي يظهر عندي أنه أشار إلى الجاهلية التي يخصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and almsgiving receive a special command as bodily and financial pillars, then fall within the general command to obey; purification from sin and adornment with piety are expressed through a repellent metaphor.
rows.anchor: وأقمن الصلاة: أمرهن أمرا خاصا بالصلاة والزكاة، إذ هما عمودا الطاعة البدنية والمالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor of filth and purity deters from prohibited acts and encourages obedience; rijs can mean sin, punishment, impurity, or defects, all removed from the household.
rows.anchor: والرجس يقع على الإثم، وعلى العذاب، وعلى النجاسة، وعلى النقائص، فأذهب الله جميع ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets rijs here as associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الرجس هنا: الشرك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says rijs means sin.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: الإثم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets rijs as Satan.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الشيطان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses rijs as transgression.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الفسق

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports an interpretation of rijs as all sins; other reported glosses include doubt, miserliness, innate disposition, desires, and innovations.
rows.anchor: ذكره الماوردي. وقيل: الشك وقيل: البخل والطبع وقيل: الأهواء والبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl is parsed as vocative, praise, or specification; the author notes specification is uncommon when addressing someone and cites poetic constructions.
rows.anchor: وانتصب أهل على النداء، أو على المدح، أو على الاختصاص، وهو قليل في المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the household includes the wives and the Prophet’s male relatives, Arabic uses masculine plural pronouns for the mixed group.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أهل البيت يشملهن وآباءهن، غلب المذكر على المؤنث في الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the view of ʿIkrima, Muqātil, and Ibn al-Sāʾib that Ahl al-Bayt means only the Prophet’s wives: the masculine pronouns contradict that reading, and the Ibn ʿAbbas attribution may be unsound.
rows.anchor: أن أهل البيت في هذه الآية مختص بزوجاته عليه ليس بجيد

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says the verse specifically includes the Prophet, ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn; similar reports come from Anas, ʿĀʾisha, and Umm Salama.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري: هو خاص برسول الله وعلي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk includes the Prophet’s family and wives.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هم أهله وأزواجه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم والثعلبي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam and al-Thaʿlabī identify the household as the Hāshimite relatives barred from alms: the families of ʿAbbās, ʿAlī, ʿAqīl, and Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أرقم، والثعلبي: بنو هاشم الذين يحرمون الصدقة آل عباس، وآل علي، وآل عقيل، وآل جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān concludes that the wives and family are included; the wives especially merit the name because they constantly lived in the Prophet’s house.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أنهم زوجاته وأهله، فلا تخرج الزوجات عن أهل البيت، بل يظهر أنهن أحق بهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the wives are certainly included, together with the Prophet’s daughter, her sons, and her husband.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والذي يظهر أن زوجاته لا يخرجن عن ذلك البتة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also takes the verse as evidence that the Prophet’s wives belong to his household and says their homes received revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وفي هذا دليل على أن نساء النبي من أهل بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connection of remember with the preceding address supports including the wives in the household; those excluding them treat this as a new address.
rows.anchor: واتصال واذكرن بما قبله يدل على أنهن من البيت، ومن لم يدخلهن قال: هي ابتداء مخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember may mean retain and recall the revelations or recount and transmit them to others.
rows.anchor: واذكرن، إما بمعنى احفظن وتذكرنه، وإما اذكرنه لغيركن واروينه حتى ينقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the Qurʾan and wisdom is the Prophet’s non-Qurʾanic sayings and practice, though wisdom may instead describe the signs.
rows.anchor: ومن آيات الله: هو القرآن، والحكمة: هي ما كان من حديثه وسنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description gentle softens the tone, while all-knowing warns the audience.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: لطيفا، تليين، وفي خبيرا، تحذير ما

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the verb with feminine agreement, while the majority read it with masculine agreement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: ما تتلى بتاء التأنيث، والجمهور: بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet’s wives, or Umm Salama specifically, asked why the Qurʾan mentioned men but not women; another report says Muslim women asked after revelations about the Prophet’s wives, and this verse followed.
rows.anchor: وروي أن نساءه عليه الصلاة والسلام، قلن: يا رسول الله، ذكر الله الرجال في القرآن ولم يذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten qualities move from outward submission to faith and the virtues contained within them, ending with constant awareness of God; the two specified objects emphasize guarding sexual honor and remembering God by His comprehensive name.
rows.anchor: فبدأ أولا بالانقياد الظاهر، ثم بالتصديق، ثم بالأوصاف التي بعدهما تندرج في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of guarding and remembering are omitted in the feminine clauses because the preceding masculine clauses supply them; masculine plural agreement includes women in the promised reward.
rows.anchor: وحذف من الحافظات والذاكرات المفعول لدلالة ما تقدم

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: The majority, including Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatāda, and Mujāhid, report that the Prophet proposed Zaynab bint Jaḥsh for Zayd; she initially refused, then accepted after the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور، وابن عباس، وقتادة، ومجاهد، وغيرهم: خطب الرسول لزيد زينب بنت جحش، فأبت

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd instead says Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqba offered herself to the Prophet, who gave her in marriage to Zayd; she and her brother objected, and the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: وهبت أم كلثوم بنت عقبة بن أبي معيط، وهي أول امرأة وهبت للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān judges the first account more sound and links the verse to the preceding list of Muslim virtues, correcting those who refused the Prophet’s direction because obedience to him is obedience to God.
rows.anchor: والسبب الأول أصح. ومناسبة هذه الآية أنه لما ذكر تلك الأوصاف السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayra is an irregular verbal noun from choosing; one reading has a quiescent yāʾ, and the verb is read with feminine agreement by named readers and masculine agreement by others.
rows.anchor: والخيرة: مصدر من تخير على غير قياس، كالطيرة من تطير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the pronoun should grammatically have been singular after the negated singular pair; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because coordination with wa requires a plural unless ellipsis is assumed.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كان من حق الضمير أن يوحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipient is Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, whom God favored with Islam and the Prophet favored by freeing him; his wife was Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, whom the Prophet had proposed for him.
rows.anchor: للذي أنعم الله عليه، بالإسلام، وهو أجل النعم، وهو زيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says God favored Zayd with the Prophet’s companionship and affection, and the Prophet favored him by adopting him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أنعم الله عليه بصحبتك ومودتك، وأنعمت عليه بتبنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Zayd complained that Zaynab’s rank made life difficult and her speech hurt him, the Prophet asked whether anything about her troubled him and told him to keep her and fear God in their treatment.
rows.anchor:
فقال:
«أرابك منها شيء؟» قال: لا والله ولكنها تعظم علي لشرفها وتؤذيني بلسانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to retain Zaynab was a recommendation against divorce; Zayd divorced her, and the Prophet married her after her waiting period ended.
rows.anchor: أمسك عليك زوجك» ، أي لا تطلقها، وهو أمر ندب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated purpose was to remove hardship for believers marrying the divorced wives of adopted sons; such women are not prohibited like the wives of biological sons.
rows.anchor: لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أن يتزوجوا زوجات من كانوا تبنوه

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn says God had revealed that Zayd would divorce Zaynab and that the Prophet would marry her by divine marriage; when Zayd complained and announced his intent to divorce, the narrative continues in the following segment.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن الحسين: كان قد أوحى الله إليه أن زيدا سيطلقها

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: In ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn’s account, the Prophet said keep your wife as counsel while knowing Zayd would divorce her; he concealed knowledge that God would reveal and feared public gossip about marrying his freedman’s former wife.
rows.anchor:
على طريق الأدب والوصية، وهو يعلم أنه سيطلقها.
وهذا هو الذي أخفى في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān endorses this account as the position of leading investigators; the Prophet feared hypocrites’ slander about marrying an adopted son’s former wife, and God reminded him that He is more deserving of fear.
rows.anchor:
وهذا المروي عن علي بن الحسين
، هو الذي عليه أهل التحقيق من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is protected in his movements and stillness; Abū Ḥayyān rejects interpretations that diminish prophethood and sets aside some exegetes’ unsound claims.
rows.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم في حركاته وسكناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes God or the Prophet address Zayd: Zayd concealed attraction to Zaynab while showing disinterest, fearing the Prophet wanted her for himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل قوله واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه: خطاب من الله عز وجل، أو من النبي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that concealed desire for a permissible woman and marrying her lawfully are not blameworthy, especially where the marriage serves wider religious benefit and no one is harmed.
rows.anchor: فهذا من ذلك القبيل، لأن طموح قلب الإنسان إلى بعض مشتهياته، من امرأة أو غيرها، غير موصوف بالقبح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites the early Medinan practice of Anṣār giving one of two wives to a Muhājir as evidence that a friend’s marrying a woman released by her husband was not socially shocking.
rows.anchor: فإن المهاجرين حين دخلوا المدينة، استهم الأنصار بكل شيء، حتى أن الرجل منهم إذا كانت له امرأتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lists Zaynab’s security, honor, and place among the Mothers of the Believers, plus the general removal of hardship, as benefits of the marriage.
rows.anchor: الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أمنت الأئمة والضيعة ونالت الشرف وعادت أما من أمهات المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction keep your wife, عليك reaches the attached pronoun with a preposition referring to the same person; Abū Ḥayyān cites parallel poetry and Qurʾanic phrases and treats the preposition as a noun in such constructions.
rows.anchor: أمسك عليك فيه وصول الفعل الرافع الضمير المتصل إلى الضمير المجرور وهما لشخص واحد

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥūfī treats hide in yourself as a new clause and fear as coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: وتخفي في نفسك: مستأنف، وتخشى: معطوف على وتخفي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the waw as circumstantial or coordinating, supplying alternative relations among the Prophet’s command to retain Zaynab, concealment, and fear of public talk.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: واو الحال، أي تقول لزيد: أمسك عليك زوجك، مخفيا في نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects making the positive imperfect clause a circumstantial phrase with an unexpressed subject, since this is rare and unsuitable as a grammatical rule.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون وتخفي حالا على إضمار مبتدأ، أي وأنت تخفي، لأنه مضارع مثبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses Zayd’s completed need with Zaynab as intercourse.
rows.anchor: فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا: أي حاجة، قيل: وهو الجماع، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عصمة نوح بن أبي مريم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abū ʿIṣma, Nūḥ ibn Abī Maryam, says Zaynab stated that she had not refused Zayd herself but God had prevented him from her; other reports say he could not consummate the marriage.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو عصمة: نوح بن أبي مريم، بإسناد رفعه إلى زينب أنها قالت: ما كنت أمتنع منه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the completed need as the divorce.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الوطر هنا: الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have We married her to you; Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and ʿAlī read I married her to you.
rows.anchor:
وقرأ الجمهور:
زوجناكها، بنون العظمة
وجعفر بن محمد، وابن الحنفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse removes the ban on marrying an adopted son’s former wife after marital ties end.
rows.anchor: ونفى تعالى الحرج عن المؤمنين في إجراء أزواج المتبنين مجرى أزواج البنين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says God’s command is eternal and so cannot properly be called something brought into being; he allows with difficulty that it could mean one of the things commanded into action.
rows.anchor:
قال ابن عطية: وإلا فالأمر
قديم لا يوصف بأنه مفعول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets the command as God’s intended creation, necessarily realized, exemplified by the Prophet’s marriage to Zaynab.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وكان أمر الله الذي يريد أن يكونه، مفعولا: مكونا لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet is included in the general removal of hardship for believers, the verse separately removes hardship for him as honor and distinction.
rows.anchor: ولما نفى الحرج عن المؤمنين فيما ذكر، واندرج الرسول فيهم، إذ هو سيد المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says what God prescribed for the Prophet includes a valid marriage without a dowry.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: فيما خص به من صحة النكاح بلا صداق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the phrase means what God made lawful for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: فيما أحل له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the special allowance to include marrying more than four wives; the author connects the reference to prophetic precedent and reports large numbers of wives and concubines for Solomon and David.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: في الزيادة على الأربع، وكانت اليهود عابوه بكثرة النكاح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the phrase about God’s way as a verbal noun or source; other proposed parses include an implied command or exhortation.
rows.anchor: وانتصب سنة الله على أنه اسم موضوع موضع المصدر، قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that exhortation is not a sound parse: the governing word cannot be omitted, and exhortation cannot target an absent third person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقوله: أو على الإغراء، ليس بجيد، لأن عامل الاسم في الإغراء لا يجوز حذفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who passed before are the prophets, as shown by the following description that they conveyed God’s messages.
rows.anchor: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command means His decrees and created events; مقدورا means possessing measure, proceeding by measure, or a settled and fixed decree.
rows.anchor: وكان أمر الله: أي مأموراته، والكائنات من أمره، فهي مقدورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may modify those who passed before or be an independent subject, with praise as another possible parse; Ibn ʿAbd Allāh reads it as a past verb and Ubayy as a singular message.
rows.anchor: والذين: صفة للذين خلوا، أو مرفوع، أو منصوب على إضمارهم، أو على أمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God as ḥasīb can mean the one who reckons deeds and beliefs or the one sufficient for people.
rows.anchor: وكفى بالله حسيبا: أي محاسبا على جميع الأعمال والعقائد، أو محسبا: أي كافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point of saying Muhammad is not the father of the community’s men is to deny adoption-based affinal and marriage consequences, not to assert he had no surviving son or to argue about the ages of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn.
rows.anchor: ثم نفى تعالى كون رسوله أبا أحد من رجالكم، بينه وبين من تبناه من حرمة الصهارة والنكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the light form of lākin and an implied kāna before Messenger; ʿAbd al-Wārith reads the emphatic form with an implied predicate, while Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it lightly with nominative predicates.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ولكن رسول، بتخفيف لكن ونصب رسول على إضمار كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read khātam with kasra, meaning Muhammad brought the prophets to a close; poetic evidence illustrates ellipsis of the predicate after lākin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: خاتم، بكسر التاء، بمعنى أنه ختمهم، أي جاء آخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Muhammad called himself the seal of a thousand prophets and the brick completing a building, along with other explicit reports, establish that no prophet follows him.
rows.anchor:
وروي عنه أنه قال: أنا خاتم ألف نبي
وعنه: أنا خاتم النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ descent at the end of time does not contradict finality: he was commissioned before Muhammad and will follow Muhammad’s law and prayer direction as a member of his community.
rows.anchor: ولا يرد نزول عيسى آخر الزمان، لأنه ممن نبئ قبله، وينزل عاملا على شريعة محمد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ṭayyib’s possible ambiguity in the verse weak and warns against al-Ghazālī’s approach to finality because it could unsettle Muslims’ certainty.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وما ذكره القاضي أبو الطيب في كتابه المسمى بالهداية، من تجويز الاحتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening reading means the prophets were sealed by Muhammad, like a seal or stamp; anyone claiming acquired continuing prophethood or a saint superior to a prophet is an apostate, and the author recounts a claimant executed in Málaga.
rows.anchor:
وقرأ الحسن، والشعبي، وزيد بن علي، والأعرج: بخلاف وعاصم: بفتح التاء بمعنى:
أنهم به ختموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says constant remembrance means never forgetting God; glorification is included in remembrance but singled out as among its best forms.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أن لا ينساه أبدا، أو التسبيح مندرج في الذكر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda recommends saying the familiar declarations of God’s glory, praise, oneness, greatness, and powerlessness to act without Him.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: قولوا سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says ritually pure and sexually impure people may say these formulas.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد: هذه الكلمات يقولها الطاهر والجنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening may stand for remembrance throughout all time by naming its two ends; Ibn ʿAbbās instead specifies dawn and night prayers, al-Akhfash the period between afternoon and evening, and Qatāda dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: والوقتان كناية عن جميع الزمان، ذكر الطرفين إشعار بالاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance may encompass every act of obedience; the author then singles out prayer as glorification, especially dawn and night prayers because they are harder to perform.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأمر بالذكر وإكثاره تكثير الطاعات والإقبال على الطاعات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets God’s prayer for believers as mercy; Ibn Jubayr says forgiveness, Abū al-ʿĀliya says praise, and another view says compassion.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يصلي عليكم: يرحمكم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the angels’ prayer is seeking forgiveness, while Muqātil says it is supplication; the author explains God guides believers from disobedience to obedience by mercy and calls to remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الدعاء، والمعنى: هو الذي يترحم عليكم، حيث يدعوكم إلى الخير

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the movement from darkness to light as guidance from error to right guidance; Muqātil says from disbelief to faith, while other reports say from Hell to Paradise or from graves to resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من الضلالة إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s and the angels’ prayers differ in their acts but share the intended good: God wills to deliver it through mercy and angels through seeking forgiveness; this is clearer than al-Zamakhshari’s mixture of literal and figurative agency.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الله غير صلاة الملائكة، فكيف اشتركا في قدر مشترك؟ وهو إرادة وصول الخير إليهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the angels as if they caused mercy because their prayers are answered and reads believers’ prayer for the Prophet as supplication that God bless him.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جعلوا لكونهم مستجابي الدعوة، كأنهم فاعلون الرحمة والرأفة

rows.speaker: الرقاشي
rows.claim: Al-Raqāshī says God greets believers on the Day they meet Him by saying peace to servants who pleased Him through obedience.
rows.anchor: يقول للمؤمنين: السلام عليكم، مرحبا بعبادي الذين أرضوني باتباع أمري، قاله الرقاشي

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib says the angel of death does not take a believer’s soul before greeting him.
rows.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب: معناه أن ملك الموت لا يقبض روح المؤمن حتى يسلم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the angel of death tells a believer that his Lord sends peace before taking his soul; this reading leaves the pronoun’s referent unstated.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: إذا جاء ملك الموت لقبض روح المؤمن قال: ربك يقرؤك السلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says believers greet one another with peace on entering Paradise, safe from every fear; other reports place the greeting at resurrection or among the angels.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يوم دخولهم الجنة يحيي بعضهم بعضا بالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say angels greet believers at that time, or the angel of death and his companions announce Paradise; the grammar treats the greeting as directed to its recipients except where it is mutual greeting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو سلام ملك الموت والملائكة معه عليهم، وبشارتهم بالجنة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad distinguishes a greeting as a prayer from salām as a particular form of peace, citing the description of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفرق المبرد بين التحية والسلام فقال: التحية يكون ذلك دعاء، والسلام مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generous reward is Paradise.
rows.anchor: والأجر الكريم: الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a witness regarding those to whom he was sent, their denial or belief, and the delivery of his message; witness may also refer to conveying the testimony of earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: شاهدا على من بعثت إليهم، وعلى تكذيبهم وتصديقهم، أي مفعولا قولك عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness is a prospective circumstantial phrase because the Prophet becomes a witness when he bears and gives testimony; alternatively, testimony of belief and denial occurred together in the prophetic mission’s time.
rows.anchor: وانتصب شاهدا على أنه حال مقدرة، إذا كان قولك عند الله وقت الإرسال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses calling to God as calling people to affirm that there is no god but God; Ibn ʿĪsā says it means calling to obedience.
rows.anchor: وداعيا إلى الله، قال ابن عباس: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By His permission means that God makes the difficult call from polytheism to monotheism possible, not merely that He formally authorized it.
rows.anchor: بإذنه: أي بتسهيله وتيسيره، ولا يراد به حقيقة الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is an illuminating lamp because he dispels polytheism’s darkness and guides the lost as a lamp guides sight; God’s prophetic light illuminates understanding.
rows.anchor: وسراجا منيرا: جلى من ظلمات الشرك، واهتدى به الضالون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj coordinates illuminating lamp with witness, construing the phrase as an illuminating book; al-Farrāʾ reads it as reciting an illuminating lamp.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو معطوف على شاهدا، أي وذا سراج منير، أي كتاب نير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the phrase to coordinate with the object of sent you; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because the resulting meaning sends the Qurʾan, which is described as revealed, not sent.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز على هذا التفسير أن يعطف على كاف أرسلناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to give good news follows from the Prophet’s mission as witness, herald, warner, and caller; the great bounty may mean reward, added reward, favor over other peoples, or Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى أنه أرسل نبيه شاهدا إلى آخره، تضمن ذلك الأمر بتلك الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns heeding disbelievers’ and hypocrites’ improper requests or deceptive advice; leaving their harm means refraining from punishing them, though the sword verse abrogated this for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين: نهي له عليه السلام عن السماع منهم في أشياء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets leaving their harm as leaving retaliation for their harm to the Prophet until commanded otherwise.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing Zayd and Zaynab’s consummated marriage and her waiting period, the text clarifies that a woman divorced before intercourse owes no waiting period.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى قصة زيد وزينب وتطليقه إياها، وكانت مدخولا بها، واعتدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here marrying means concluding a marriage contract, named for the intercourse it leads to; the Qurʾan generally reserves the term for the contract and uses euphemisms for intercourse, except in 2:230.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نكحتم: عقدتم عليهن. وسمي العقد نكاحا لأنه سبب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although scriptural women share the rule, believers are specified to signal that a Muslim should choose a believing woman; then includes both immediate and delayed divorce after marriage.
rows.anchor: والكتابيات، وإن شاركت المؤمنات في هذا الحكم، فتخصيص المؤمنات بالذكر تنبيه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says then removes doubt that the waiting-period rule differs when divorce follows the contract quickly rather than after a long marriage; Abū Ḥayyān objects to his use of the construction with من عسى or allows it as common usage.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نفى التوهم عمن عسى يتوهم تفاوت الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent rule is that divorce requires an existing marriage contract; the majority among Companions and Successors reject divorce directed at a woman before marriage, while a large group including Mālik permits it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الطلاق لا يكون إلا بعد العقد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of touch is intercourse and mere seclusion does not count, while Abū Ḥanīfa and his associates treat valid seclusion like intercourse.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه: حكم الخلوة الصحيحة حكم المسيس

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dāwūd says a revocably divorced wife who is taken back and divorced again before intercourse need not complete the first waiting period or begin a new one.
rows.anchor: قال داود. وقال عطاء وجماعة: تمضي في عدتها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and others, with one Shāfiʿī position, say she completes the waiting period from the first divorce; Mālik and most regional jurists require a new waiting period from the second divorce.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وجماعة: تمضي في عدتها عن طلاقها الأول

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: For a definitively separated woman remarried during her waiting period and divorced before intercourse, Dāwūd says there is no waiting period from either marriage and she receives half the dowry; another group completes the first waiting period, while a third requires full dowry and a new period.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أيضا أنها لو كانت بائنا غير مبتوتة، فتزوجها في العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading of تعتدونها uses the intensified form from counting, meaning to complete the number of days; a light form is transmitted from Ibn Kathīr and other Meccans, and Abū Ḥayyān rejects calling that transmission an error.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تعتدونها، بتشديد الدال: افتعل من العد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests the light reading derives from injustice or transgression against women; Abū Ḥayyān notes that, despite its usual preposition, the verb can take a direct object.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وروي عن أبي برزة، عن ابن كثير: بتخفيف الدال من العدوان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the light form as count against them, with the omitted preposition supplied; he connects it to the ban on retaining wives to harm them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقرئ: تعتدونها مخففا، أي تعتدون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The released woman is apparently entitled to a parting gift whether or not a dowry was specified; the command seems obligatory, though some say recommended.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن من طلقت قبل المسيس لها المتعة مطلقا، سواء كانت ممدودة أم مفروضا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gracious release means kind words without harm or withholding what is owed; another view says not to demand back what was given.
rows.anchor: والسراج الجميل: هو كلمة طيبة دون أذى ولا منع واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from believers’ marriage rules to the Prophet’s wives; their wages are dowries, and paying them promptly is preferred because it clears the husband’s debt and avoids enjoyment without delivered compensation.
rows.anchor: والأجور: المهور، لأنه أجر على الاستمتاع بالبضع وغيره مما يجوز به الاستمتاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The early Muslims customarily paid dowries immediately; the Prophet asked a Companion who lacked means where his iron armor was.
rows.anchor: والتعجيل كان سنة السلف، لا يعرف منهم غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier that God granted the Prophet among those owned by the right hand favors captured women from enemy territory over purchased imports; the text calls the former good and the latter bad, while God’s fayʾ denotes what is wholesome.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تخصيص ما ملكت يمينه بقوله: مما أفاء الله عليك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the Prophet’s permitted wives broadly to include those married with or without dowry and the other named categories; Abū Ḥayyān first calls the narrower reading apparent, then notes it restricts the later pronoun, while Ibn Zayd’s reading carries it through the list.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أي من تزوجها بمهر، ومن تزوجها بلا مهر، وجميع النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording what right do you have indicates the husband’s right in the waiting period predominates, though he cannot waive God’s right to it.
rows.anchor: وقوله: فما لكم يدل على أن العدة حق الزوج فيها غالب، وإن كانت لا تسقط بإسقاطه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet could marry whichever women he wished, which distressed his wives; once the verse restricted him, they were relieved because the remaining eligible categories were few.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتزوج أي النساء شاء، وكان ذلك يشق على نسائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The link between permission to defer or receive wives and the later ban on taking others reads smoothly if the pronoun means only the wives named as lawful, supporting a consistent reading of the passage.
rows.anchor: ثم مجيء ترجي من تشاء منهن، إشارة إلى ما تقدم، ثم مجيء ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Umm Hāniʾ says the Prophet proposed to her, but she declined and was excused; she understood this verse to make her forbidden to him because she had not emigrated with him and was among those pardoned at the conquest.
rows.anchor: قالت أم هانىء، بنت أبي طالب: خطبني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī records two positions on the migration condition: it applies to all wives, or only to the Prophet’s female relatives listed in the verse.
rows.anchor: وحكى الماوردي في ذلك قولين: أحدهما: أن الهجرة شرط في إحلال الأزواج على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration companionship means sharing in the act of migration, not necessarily travelling at the same time; plural uncles and aunts are expressed with singular generic nouns.
rows.anchor:
والمعية هنا:
الاشتراك في الهجرة لا في الصحبة فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet had none of the women who gave themselves to him as wives.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس: لم يكن عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحد منهن بالهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says four women offered themselves, including Maymūna and the women already mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الموهبات أربع: ميمونة بنت الحارث، ومن ذكر معها قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read wife in the accusative and if she offers with a broken hamza: God permits her if she offers herself and the Prophet intends to marry her; his intention completes acceptance of the gift.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وامرأت، بالنصب إن وهبت، بكسر الهمزة: أي أحللناها لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When two conditions occur, the second is a condition within the first, logically preceding it unless context establishes another order; the grammatical issue has detailed disagreements.
rows.anchor: وإذا اجتمع شرطان، فالثاني شرط في الأول، متأخر في اللفظ، متقدم في الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads wife as a nominative subject with an omitted predicate; Ubayy and other readers open the hamza, referring to a particular woman already offering, while Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads it with since, also for a particular past case.
rows.anchor:
وقرأ أبو
حيوة: وامرأة مؤمنة، بالرفع على الابتداء، والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Switching from direct address to the Prophet in the conditional and back to direct address marks his special privilege; repeating Prophet honors and establishes his right by virtue of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الخطاب إلى الغيبة في النبي، إن أراد النبي، ثم رجع إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority require a marriage contract to use neither hire nor gift wording; al-Karkhī allows hire wording, but the author reports the response that a temporary lease conflicts with permanent marriage.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: على أن التزويج لا يجوز بلفظ الإجارة ولا بلفظ الهبة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وصاحباه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his two companions permit a marriage contract in gift wording if the woman offers herself and the groom stipulates a dowry; they say the Prophet and his community share rulings absent proof of a special rule.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة وصاحباه إلى جواز عقد النكاح بلفظ الهبة إذا وهبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority respond that both the meaning and wording of self-gifting are special to the Prophet, since wording follows meaning and those claiming shared wording need evidence.
rows.anchor:
وحجة الجمهور:
أنه، عليه السلام، خص بمعنى الهبة ولفظها جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read خالصة in the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun meaning exclusively or purely; a nominative reading is also transmitted and can mean this is a privilege for you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: خالصة، بالنصب، وهو مصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says active participles can readily function as verbal nouns; Abū Ḥayyān objects that such forms are rare and challenges the cited examples, including a line by al-Farazdaq.
rows.anchor:
وقال الزمخشري:
والفاعل والفاعلة في المصادر على غير عزيزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes the privilege describe the woman who offers herself: accusative خالصة is a circumstantial phrase, while nominative makes it the predicate, both limiting self-gifting to the Prophet; scholars agree others cannot use this arrangement.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: خالصة لك من صفة الواهبة نفسها لك

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s wording suggests the privilege covers all the permissions in the verse, not only the self-gift.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من كلام أبي بن كعب أن معنى قوله: خالصة لك يراد به جميع هذه الإباحة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the later statement about what was prescribed for the community as an inserted proof that the listed marriage permissions are uniquely the Prophet’s.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والدليل على أنها وردت في أثر الإحلالات الأربع مخصوصة برسول الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the privilege removes religious constraint and gives the Prophet the preferable options in worldly life; if خالصة describes the woman, she is uniquely available to him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لكيلا يكون عليك حرج: أي لكيلا يكون عليك ضيق في دينك

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the clarification prevents people from thinking the Prophet sinned and reassures all believers of God’s forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لكيلا يكون، أي بينا هذا البيان وشرحنا هذا الشرح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God forgives one who falls into hardship if he repents and is merciful by granting ease; Abū Ḥayyān detects a Muʿtazilite implication.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: غفورا للواقع في الحرج إذا تاب، رحيما بالتوسعة على عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about what was prescribed means the Prophet’s marriage rules differ from the community’s; it prevents believers from imitating his special marriage and concubinage allowances.
rows.anchor: قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم الآية، معناه: أن ما ذكرنا فرضك وحكمك مع نسائك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the community’s prescribed limit is no more than four wives; Qatāda says their rules include a guardian, witnesses, and dowry, while another view adds maintenance and clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ما فرضنا عليهم، هو أن لا يجاوزوا أربعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view permits ownership of a woman only if she may lawfully be captured; another permits unnumbered concubines alongside four free wives, with the law reflecting what is best for both Prophet and community.
rows.anchor: وما ملكت أيمانهم، قيل: لا يثبت الملك إلا إذا كانت ممن يجوز سبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet’s wives sought more maintenance, so he left them for a month; when given a choice and fearing divorce, they asked him to prescribe whatever he wished from himself and his property.
rows.anchor: روي أن أزواجه عليه السلام لما تغايرن وابتغين زيادة النفقة، فهجرهن شهرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: The pronoun in among them apparently returns to the Prophet’s wives; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan understand the choice as divorcing whichever he wished or keeping her.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والحسن: في طلاق ممن تشاء ممن حصل في عصمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group reads the choice as marrying whichever self-offering woman he wished or postponing her; Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say it means varying the wives’ turns, delaying or increasing them as he wished.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: في تزوج من تشاء من الواهبات، وتأخير من تشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the wives knew this discretion came from God, jealousy and resentment would ease and they would be content; this suits the reported occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: فإذا علمن أن هذا حكم الله وقضاؤه، زالت الإحنة والغيرة عنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of several readings of taking back a woman previously set aside, Abū Ḥayyān prefers the straightforward sense: seeking again one of the wives from whom he had withdrawn.
rows.anchor: والراجح القول الأول

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase includes replacing a deceased wife or one released, without exceeding the number of wives already present.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: المعنى: من مات من نسائك اللواتي عندك، أو خليت سبيلها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lists possible applications: choose whom to approach or leave, divorce or retain, divide time or not, or set aside a concubine and marry another.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: بمعنى تترك مضاجع من تشاء منهن وتضاجع من تشاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that when the Prophet proposed to a woman, no one else could propose to her until he left her.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: كان النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا خطب امرأة لم يكن لأحد أن يخطبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report names Sawda, Juwayriyya, Ṣafiyya, Maymūna, and Umm Ḥabība as deferred, and ʿĀʾisha, Ḥafṣa, Umm Salama, and Zaynab as received; another says he divided equally except Sawda, who gave her turn to ʿĀʾisha to remain one of his wives.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه أرجأ منهن: سودة، وجويرية، وصفية، وميمونة، وأم حبيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delegating the choice to the Prophet reassures the wives when they know it comes from God, since they stand equally in this matter.
rows.anchor: انتهى. ذلك التفويض إلى مشيئتك أدنى إلى قرة عيونهن وانتفاء حزنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers parse their eyes be gladdened actively; Ibn Muḥayṣin reads it as a causative form with their eyes accusative, another reading makes it passive, and the majority use all of them as an emphatic nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أن تقر أعينهن: مبنيا للفاعل من قرت العين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes what is in your hearts to point especially to the Prophet’s love for one wife over another, while including the believers more generally.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والإشارة به هاهنا إلى ما في قلب رسول الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وعبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and ʿUbayda apply the statement to a wife who resents God’s arrangement, and urge the wives to agree and seek the Prophet’s happiness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري، وعبيدة: من لم يرض منهن بما يريد الله من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the hearts and is forbearing toward feelings that arise involuntarily; reports agree the Prophet maintained equal turns until death, except for Sawda’s gift.
rows.anchor: واتفقت الروايات على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام، كان يعدل بينهن في القسمة حتى مات

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب والحسن وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ubayy, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn, and others hold that the ban on further wives is decisive and remains in force; they disagree on what after refers to.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنها محكمة، وهو قول أبي بن كعب وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبي وعكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ubayy, ʿIkrima, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say after means after the women made lawful in the preceding verse, so no additional Arab, non-Arab, scriptural, or slave wife by marriage is permitted.
rows.anchor: فقال أبي، وعكرمة، والضحاك: ومن بعد اللواتي أحللنا لك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say after means after the Prophet’s nine-wife limit: God rewarded the wives for choosing Him and His Messenger by barring replacements and rescinding the earlier broader permission.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وقتادة: من بعد، لأن التسع نصاب رسول الله من الأزواج

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جبير وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn Jubayr, and a report from ʿIkrima say the Prophet could no longer marry Jewish or Christian women or replace Muslim wives with them.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وابن جبير: وروي عن عكرمة: من بعد، أي من بعد إباحة النساء على العموم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets exchanging wives as a pre-Islamic custom in which two men swapped wives; al-Ṭabarī and others reject this because Arabs never practiced it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في قوله ولا أن تبدل، هو من البدل الذي كان في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra min strengthens the negation by excluding the entire class of wives; the report about ʿUyayna offering to give the Prophet his wife was not a real exchange but an insult toward young ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: ومن في من أزواج زائدة لتأكيد النفي، وفائدته

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the restriction was later lifted before the Prophet died, as also reported from Umm Salama and attributed to ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة: ما مات حتى حل له النساء

rows.speaker: هبة الله الضرير
rows.claim: Hibat Allāh al-Ḍarīr says the permission in ترجي من تشاء abrogated the ban and that this is the Qurʾan’s only case of a later verse abrogating an earlier one.
rows.anchor: وقيل بالقرآن، وهو قوله: ترجي من تشاء منهن الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya criticizes this abrogation argument; another view says the earlier permission to marry the listed women came later in revelation despite its earlier position in the written order, and Ibn ʿAbbās is reported on both sides.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وكلامه يضعف من جهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, wife of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, is proposed as a woman whose beauty might attract the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل: منهن أسماء بنت عميس الخثعمية، امرأة جعفر بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches the beauty clause circumstantially to the subject of replace, not the indefinite object wives; Abū Ḥayyān instead links it to an omitted general circumstance covering every case, including attraction.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري، في موضع الحال من الفاعل، وهو الضمير في تبدل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees the wording about admiring beauty as evidence that a man may look at a woman he intends to marry; reports from al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba and Muḥammad ibn Maslama support this.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفي هذا اللفظ أعجبك حسنهن، دليل على جواز أن ينظر الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owned women are excepted from the prohibition; the parsing depends on whether the phrase denotes the class of women or is a verbal noun, and Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s non-gender analysis because owned women are still women.
rows.anchor: إلا ما ملكت يمينك: أي فإنه يحل لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the exception denotes owned women as a class, nominative substitution is preferred though accusative is possible; if read as a verbal noun, Abū Ḥayyān challenges Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s claim that accusative is required, noting the competing grammatical rules and Mālik’s gloss as owned women.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان بمعنى مملوك صار من جملة النساء لأنه لم يرد حقيقة المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s watching means He preserves, witnesses, and knows everything, warning against exceeding His lawful bounds.
rows.anchor: وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا: أي راقبا، أو مراقبا، ومعناه: حافظ وشاهد ومطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says that after the meal at the Prophet’s wedding to Zaynab, guests remained talking as he tried to leave; he eventually left and returned, and a curtain was placed between him and Anas before this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين، أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما تزوج زينب بنت جحش، دعا القوم فطعموا
